md: - **First ARC on Lokpal and Lokayukta:** it recommended a Lokpal at the Union (Centre) level and Lokayuktas in the States.
- **Venue of PM's projects:** PM Narendra Modi launched the projects worth about ₹17,900 crore at **Bhogapuram** (Vizianagaram district) on 1 August 2026, at the dedication of the new airport.
- **Tilaka Manjari:** a Sanskrit prose romance written by **Dhanapala**, a Jain poet at the Paramara court (Munja and Bhoja), c. 1000 CE.
- **Muziris:** the Periplus describes Muziris, on the Malabar coast (Kerala), as a port abounding with ships from Arabia and Greece.
- **Crafts:** good roads and state incentives encouraged crafts in the Mauryan period.
- **Heavy taxation:** Kosambi also points to very heavy taxes, raised even on actors and prostitutes, as a sign of the money crisis of the later Mauryas.
- **Other coins:** Kanishka's coins show the Buddha; Mahmud of Ghazni issued silver coins with Arabic and Sanskrit legends.
- **NMHC site:** The National Maritime Heritage Complex (NMHC) is being built at **Lothal**, Gujarat, the Harappan port town.
- **Upanishads = Vedanta:** the Upanishads are called **Vedanta** ("end of the Vedas") because they come at the close of Vedic literature.
- **Kusinara and Pava (Malla):** the Buddha attained **parinirvana at Kusinara**; Mahavira died at **Pava**.

- **Little lasting political effect:** Alexander stayed in India only about 19 months; his campaign left almost no lasting political mark, while the earlier Persian rule left a deeper influence on script, art and administration.
- **Errors in Indica:** besides the wrong "no slavery" claim, Indica has uncritical tales such as gold-digging ants; Strabo, following Megasthenes, wrote that Indians did not know writing.

- **Sanskrit under the later Ikshvakus:** inscriptions of later Ikshvaku kings such as Ehuvala Chamtamula at Nagarjunakonda are in Sanskrit, so Sanskrit became prominent under the Ikshvakus after their early Prakrit records.
- **Chaitika sects:** The five Chaitika sects (Purvasaila, Aparasaila, Uttarasaila, Rajagirika, Siddharthika) were branches of the **Mahasanghikas**, founded by **Mahadeva Bhikshu**.
- **Kannada Ratnatraya:** Pampa, Ponna and Ranna are called the 'three gems' (Ratnatraya) of Kannada literature.
- **Length of the conflict:** The Rashtrakuta–Vengi (Eastern Chalukya) wars went on for about 200 years.
- **Gram Sabha (Art. 243A):** Article 243A deals with the Gram Sabha, the body of all registered voters of a village Panchayat area.
- **Intermediate tier (Art. 243B):** Under the 73rd Amendment, a State whose population does not exceed 20 lakh need not set up Panchayats at the intermediate level.
- **Temple as meeting place:** Chola temples were also the venues where village assemblies held their meetings.

- **DILRMP (modern land records):** The Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme's first phase ran from 2008 to 2016; the 2016–2026 phase brought ULPIN (Bhu-Aadhaar), a unique ID for each land parcel.
- **Khajuraho:** The Khajuraho temples of the Chandelas, such as Kandariya Mahadeva, are in the Nagara style.
- **1296 raid:** Alauddin Khalji led it while he was governor of Kara under his uncle, Sultan **Jalaluddin Khalji**, before he became Sultan himself.
- **Guru Tegh Bahadur:** called **"Hind-di-Chadar"** (Shield of India); founded **Chak Nanki** (1665), which grew into Anandpur Sahib.
- **Agra:** founded by **Sikandar Lodi** (1504); it later became a main **Mughal imperial capital** (Babur, Akbar), while Siri, Tughlaqabad and Jahanpanah were Sultanate cities of Delhi.
- **Bidriware:** metalware of a **blackened zinc alloy** (with a little copper) **inlaid with silver**.
- **Madad-i-maash:** revenue-free land grants to scholars and religious men; managed by the Sadr (Sadr-us-Sudur).
- **Classification:** historian **S. Nurul Hasan** divided Mughal zamindars into three categories – autonomous chiefs, intermediary zamindars and primary zamindars.
- **India-Brazil, July 2025:** The PM visited Brazil for the **17th BRICS Summit** (Rio de Janeiro, July 2025); ties going back to Cabral's arrival in Brazil (1500) were recalled.
- **Itsing (I-tsing):** a **Chinese** Buddhist pilgrim; visited India in 671-695 CE and studied at Nalanda.

- **Rishi movement (Kashmir):** Founded by **Sheikh Nuruddin (Nund Rishi)**, inspired by **Lal Ded (Lalla)**; it preached universal love, served people of all castes, and its followers gave up meat (vegetarianism).

- **Andhra reform line:** Before colonial rule, social reform in Andhra came through **Veerashaivism** and **Srivaishnavism**, and then Brahmanaidu, Vemana, Veerabrahmam and Nasaraiah; they opposed caste, but caste inequalities could not be removed.
- **Maratha awakening:** The Bhakti saints **Tukaram** and **Ramdas** helped create early feelings of national awakening among the Marathas, which **Shivaji** built on.
- **Sankranti in other states:** celebrated as **Pongal** in Tamil Nadu, **Magh Bihu** in Assam and **Uttarayan** in Gujarat.
- **Devotion over birth:** Bhakti saints taught that devotion, not birth or social status, decides a person's worth before God; in this way they challenged the caste hierarchy.
- **Trade secrets:** B.D. Basu also listed Indian artisans being forced to reveal their trade secrets as a cause of the ruin of Indian industry.
- **Bengal Famine 1943 – Viceroys:** it came in the last months of Lord Linlithgow and the first months of Lord Wavell (Viceroy from October 1943).
- **European troops drawn off:** On the eve of 1857 many European troops had been sent away to fight the **Crimean War** and the **Persian War**, so the sepoys greatly outnumbered them.
- **Flour rumour:** A rumour said the Company's flour was mixed with **bone dust**.
- **Chapatis:** Before the revolt, mysterious chapatis were passed from village to village across **North India**.
- **Annexations and jobs:** Annexation of princely states (such as Awadh) threw thousands of officials, retainers and soldiers of the princely courts out of work.
- **'Prophet of Indian Nationalism':** this title is given to Swami Vivekananda, not to Dayananda Saraswati.
- **Split of 1893:** In **1893**, after Dayanand's death, the Arya Samaj split into the **College (DAV) party** and the **Gurukul party**.
- **Kavi Raju:** Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary was popularly known by the title **Kavi Raju**.
- **Prakasam Barrage (Feb 2026):** automated crest-gate telemetry and SCADA were installed at the Prakasam Barrage on the Krishna at Vijayawada.
- **Treaty of Bassein (1802) – other terms:** the Peshwa ceded territory yielding about **Rs 26 lakh** a year to pay for the subsidiary force and gave up the city of **Surat** to the British.
- **Allahabad High Court:** set up in **1866** (first at Agra, moved to Allahabad in 1869) under the High Courts Act 1861 – after Canning's term ended in 1862.

- **Revenue judicial service plea (1 May 2026):** the Supreme Court issued notice on a plea for a separate "revenue judicial service" cadre; the plea, under **Article 14**, argued that revenue officers without legal training should not decide land-title disputes.
- **Significance:** The Mahad and Kalaram satyagrahas forced the national movement to confront the issue of untouchability.
- **Second RTC:** Ambedkar again demanded separate electorates for the Depressed Classes; this and other minority claims caused the communal deadlock that wrecked the conference.

- **PM-KISAN extended (2026):** On 31 July 2026 the Union Cabinet extended PM-KISAN to **2030-31** (period 2026-27 to 2030-31) with an outlay of about **Rs 3.15 lakh crore**; the Rs 6,000 a year support to farmers stays the same.
- **Roots of trusteeship:** Gandhi drew the idea from the Gita's teaching of non-possession (aparigraha) and from the English law of trusts (Snell's Equity), as he tells in his autobiography.
- **The ground:** Jallianwala Bagh was a walled garden, closed in by houses and walls, with only one narrow way in and out.
- **Other name:** The **Indian National Army (INA)** was also called the **Azad Hind Fauj**; it was the army of the Azad Hind Government, which was a separate body.
- **Proclamation:** The Azad Hind proclamation **guaranteed religious liberty** and **equal rights and equal opportunities** to all citizens.
- **Criticism:** the Extremists' Hindu religious symbols (Bhavani worship, Ganesh and Shivaji festivals) kept many Muslims away, and their social outlook was comparatively orthodox.
- **Girglani Commission's task:** it examined violations of **GO 610** and the **1975 Presidential Order** in appointments to government posts.
- **Polavaram river:** Polavaram (first proposed as Ramapada Sagaram) is a multipurpose irrigation project on the **Godavari** river.
- **ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam:** both districts lie in **north coastal Andhra Pradesh**, along the Odisha border.
- **Granville Austin's book:** *The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation* (1966).
- **K.C. Wheare's book:** *Modern Constitutions* (1951).
- **Economic justice:** no discrimination on economic grounds; removing glaring inequalities in wealth, income and property.
- **Capital of Andhra State (1953):** **Kurnool**; Hyderabad became the capital when Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1956.
- **Audi alteram partem:** means 'hear the other side' – the right to be heard, a core rule of natural justice.

- **Other religion cases:** **Church of God (Full Gospel) in India (2000)** – use of loudspeakers in worship is subject to public order (noise) limits; **Ratilal Panachand Gandhi v. State of Bombay (1954)** – the State cannot interfere with essential religious practices, it may regulate only secular activities linked to religion.
- **Navtej Singh Johar (2018):** a **five-judge** Constitution Bench (CJI Dipak Misra) read down Sec. 377 IPC for consensual sex between adults.
- **Supriyo (Oct 2023):** no fundamental right to marry; legal recognition of **same-sex marriage left to Parliament**.
- **Union of India v. ADR (2002):** candidates must disclose their **criminal record, assets and educational qualifications**.
- **Electoral Bonds case (Feb 2024):** a five-judge Bench unanimously struck down the scheme for violating the **voters' right to information** under Art. 19(1)(a).
- **Article 370 judgment (Dec 2023):** the Court held Article 370 was a **temporary provision** and upheld the President's power to declare it inoperative.
- **Demonetisation case (Jan 2023):** the 2016 notification was upheld **4:1** as valid under **Section 26(2) of the RBI Act**.
- **Munro's Madras Regulations (1816):** reversed the Cornwallis separation – the **Collector** again got **magisterial and police powers**, and village heads got petty police and judicial powers.
- **Main criticism of the law:** it stifles intra-party dissent and members' free expression, yet it has not stopped mass defections (the two-thirds merger route).
- **Legislature clause:** general seats in the legislature to be shared on an **equal district-wise basis** between the regions.
- **Gentlemen's Agreement (20 Feb 1956):** Andhra side led by Andhra State CM **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** (with N. Sanjiva Reddy); Telangana side led by **B. Ramakrishna Rao**.
- **Rajaji as Premier (1937):** left **Rayalaseema out of his cabinet**; later made anti-Andhra statements.
- **JVP report and Dhar:** the JVP Committee **reaffirmed the Dhar Commission's approach** – security, unity and economic prosperity first, new linguistic provinces postponed.
- **Legacy:** its regional safeguards became a **model for the Gentlemen's Agreement (1956)**.
- **Today:** its terms on the **capital, High Court and irrigation** are still cited in Rayalaseema debates (e.g. a High Court at Kurnool).
- **Dhar Commission's mandate:** to examine the formation of **Andhra, Karnataka, Kerala and Maharashtra**, with their boundaries and consequences; Gujarat was not in its terms.
- **Gandhi in Hyderabad:** visited Hyderabad on **9 March 1934** during his Harijan tour.
- **Article 96:** the Speaker (or Deputy Speaker) shall not preside while a resolution for his removal is under consideration; he may speak and vote in the first instance, but has no casting vote.
- **M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar:** first Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha (1952–56); became Speaker in 1956 after G.V. Mavalankar's death.

- **Expert committees (not parliamentary) – reform areas:** **Nachiket Mor** – financial inclusion; **Shanta Kumar** – FCI and PDS reform (DBT for food, decentralised procurement); **Ashok Dalwai** – doubling farmers' income (value addition, land leasing); **Kasturirangan** – NEP 2020 (5+3+3+4 school structure); **Urjit Patel** – inflation targeting at 4% ± 2%.
- **Padmaja Naidu:** daughter of **Sarojini Naidu**; first woman Governor of West Bengal.
- **Madapati Hanumantha Rao:** first Chairman of the AP Legislative Council; popularly called **Andhra Pitamaha** (T. Prakasam was called Andhra Kesari).
- **Judicial review Articles:** **Article 32** gives the **Supreme Court**, and **Articles 226/227** give the **High Courts**, the power of judicial review over tribunal decisions.
- **Emergency Part:** the Emergency provisions are in **Part XVIII** (Articles 352-360) of the Constitution.
- **Oath (Art. 124(6)):** an SC judge takes the oath before the **President** or a person **appointed by the President** for this purpose.
- **Origins:** the **presidential** form of government began in the **USA**; the **parliamentary** form began in **Britain**.

- **Sashakt Panchayat-Netri Abhiyan (MoPR):** a capacity-building campaign that **strengthens the participation and leadership of elected women representatives**, so that they, not male relatives, run the panchayat.

- **Articles for simultaneous polls:** **Art. 83** = duration of the Houses of Parliament; **Art. 85** = sessions and dissolution of Parliament; **Art. 172** = duration of State Legislatures; **Art. 174** = their sessions and dissolution; **Art. 356** = President's Rule.

- **Qualification vs disqualification:** **Art. 84** = qualifications for membership of Parliament, **Art. 102** = disqualifications for Parliament; **Art. 173** and **Art. 191** = the same for State Legislatures.
- **Constituencies:** Lok Sabha and State Assembly members are elected directly from **single-member territorial constituencies** by first-past-the-post.
- **Nodal ministry:** delimitation work of the Union is handled by the **Ministry of Law and Justice** (Legislative Department), which notifies the Delimitation Commission.
- **Who registers parties:** under **Sec. 29A, RPA 1951**, an association applies to the **Election Commission of India**, which registers it as a political party.
- **Polling-station cap:** the ECI (2025) fixed a maximum of **1,200 electors** per polling station (earlier 1,500).
- **Legal basis:** the conditions for national-party recognition are laid down in **Paragraph 6B** of the Election Symbols Order, 1968.
- **Article 312 – new All India Service:** Parliament can create a new All India Service if the **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution supported by **two-thirds** of members present and voting.

- **Financial liberalisation:** in the Washington Consensus, **market-determined interest rates** are the financial-liberalisation prescription; a **competitive exchange rate** is a separate exchange-rate prescription.

- **Own tax domain:** under State Panchayat Acts the **Gram Panchayat** has the main own taxes, such as **property (house) tax**; the intermediate and district tiers depend mostly on grants, tolls and fees.
- **Award day:** the National Panchayat Awards are given every year on **24 April**, National Panchayati Raj Day.
- **Art. 279A:** provides for the **GST Council**; inserted by the **101st Amendment, 2016**.
- **Art. 305:** saves **existing laws** and laws providing for **State monopolies** from Arts 301 and 303.
- **De-reservation review (Aug 2026):** in **August 2026** the **NCSC** began a full review of the Centre's de-reservation proposals of the last three years.
- Also in the Twelfth Schedule: **parks, gardens and playgrounds**; **promotion of cultural, educational and aesthetic aspects**.

- **Gram Sabha competence (PESA s. 4(d), 4(e)):** safeguards traditions, customs, cultural identity, **community resources** and the **customary mode of dispute resolution**; **approves plans, programmes and projects** before the Panchayat takes them up.
- **Niyamgiri (2013):** the Supreme Court asked the Gram Sabhas to decide whether the bauxite mining would affect their **religious and forest rights**.
- **Thungon Committee (1988):** also recommended **constitutional recognition** of Panchayati Raj bodies.
- **State Finance Commission:** reviews the finances of **Panchayats (Art. 243-I)** and **Municipalities (Art. 243-Y)** and recommends how State taxes and grants are shared with them.

- **Ambedkar's books – themes:** *Castes in India* (1916) – genesis and mechanism of the caste system; *Annihilation of Caste* (1936) – attack on caste (anti-caste); *Who Were the Shudras?* (1946) – origin of the Shudras; *The Untouchables* (1948) – origin of untouchability.
- **ES 2025-26 on low mobility:** low social mobility **entrenches historical inequality**.
- **Why OBC demands:** dominant peasant castes such as **Marathas, Gujjars and Patels** seek OBC status mainly for **greater life chances** (jobs, education), not ritual rank.
- **SAT – full form:** SAT is the **Securities Appellate Tribunal**, set up under the **SEBI Act, 1992**; it hears appeals against orders of SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA.

- **Rules 2026 – other conditions:** foreign funds **cannot be used for proselytisation**; under prior permission, a later instalment is released only after at least **75%** of the previous instalment has been used.
- **Family and stability:** the family is the **primary agent of socialisation**; by teaching values and norms it promotes social stability.
- **Social stability (meaning):** society keeps **peace, order, harmony, continuity** and the **effective functioning of its institutions** despite social change.
- **Urbanisation and social life:** city (metropolitan) life increases **individualism**, **competition** and **social distance** between people.
- **Irawati Karve:** the first to study **Indian kinship systematically**; she called kinship the **backbone of Indian social organisation**.
- **Andre Beteille:** wrote ***Caste, Class and Power*** (1965), a study of Sripuram village in Tamil Nadu.

- **A.R. Desai and D.P. Mukerji:** Desai traced Indian **nationalism** to **socio-economic changes under colonial rule**; D.P. Mukerji held that **tradition** is essential for understanding Indian society.

- **Georg Simmel:** German sociologist who studied **social interaction and city life**; for him society exists because **individuals interact**. In his formal sociology a **dyad** is a group of **two** and a **triad** a group of **three**.

- **Max Weber (1864–1920):** Father of **Interpretative Sociology**; **Verstehen** = interpretive understanding of social action; **class, status and power** as dimensions of stratification. Four social actions: **instrumentally rational** (goals), **value-rational** (values and ethics), **affective** (emotions), **traditional** (customs and traditions).

- **Weber's authority and bureaucracy:** **traditional** authority rests on custom; **charismatic** on personality and leadership; **legal-rational** on rules. An **ideal type** is an analytical model to understand social reality. In bureaucracy, official conduct follows **written rules**, and the **merit system** bases appointment and promotion on qualifications.

- **Marx's key ideas:** **historical materialism** – the economic base shapes society, politics and culture; **surplus value** – the value workers produce beyond the wages they get; Marx is a founder of the **conflict perspective** (class struggle).

- **Marx's alienation:** from the **product** (goods are owned and sold by the capitalist), from the **production process** (forced, monotonous work), from **fellow humans** (who become competitors) and from **oneself** (one's own human nature).

- **Comte's positivism:** knowledge must rest on **observation, experimentation and scientific evidence**, not on divine or supernatural forces. In the **positive** stage, rain is explained by atmospheric processes.

- **Durkheim's concepts:** **social facts** – external forces such as laws, customs, religion and traditions that exist outside the individual and shape behaviour; **collective conscience** – shared beliefs and values that unite society; **anomie** – normlessness caused by rapid social change, seen in crime and suicide. Books: *The Division of Labour in Society*, *The Rules of Sociological Method*, *Suicide*.

- **C. Wright Mills (1916–1962):** the **sociological imagination** is the ability to connect personal experience (**biography** – one's own life and troubles) with wider social forces and **history**; e.g. one person's unemployment (personal trouble) is linked to an **economic slowdown** (public issue).
- **Aims of gender mainstreaming:** reduce gender discrimination, ensure equitable development, promote inclusive governance and women's empowerment.
- **In force:** the BNS 2023 (with the BNSS and BSA) came into force on **1 July 2024**, replacing the IPC.
- **Earlier lead countries:** under the old 14-sector set-up, **Myanmar** led **energy** (and agriculture); after the cut to 7 sectors, energy comes under India's **security** sector.
- **Ashgabat Agreement (2011):** a multimodal transport and transit corridor linking **Central Asia** with the **Persian Gulf** (via Iran and Oman); India joined in **2018**.
- **Social security in the UDHR:** the right to social security (Art. 22) is an economic and social right, like the rights to work, education and health.
- **Mission Indradhanush (2014):** immunisation drive of the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare**; not an MWCD umbrella mission.
- **Prisoners with disabilities (SC, Dec 2025):** prisons must be made accessible and **prison manuals revised** in line with the **RPwD Act, 2016**.
- **Waqf Act, 1995:** the main law for the administration of waqf properties, through State Waqf Boards, the Central Waqf Council and Waqf Tribunals.
- **Half-Lion:** 'Half-Lion: How P.V. Narasimha Rao Transformed India' (2016) is a book on Narasimha Rao by **Vinay Sitapati**.
- **Article 370:** gave **special status** to Jammu and Kashmir; operative from 17 November 1952, abrogated on 5 August 2019.
- **Mudh-Nyoma airbase:** in **eastern Ladakh**, facing the Western sector of the LAC; built by the BRO at about 13,000 ft.
- **SHe-Box routing:** a complaint filed on SHe-Box goes directly to the Internal Committee or Local Committee that has jurisdiction over it, which speeds redressal under the POSH Act.
- **Disha Bill passed:** the AP Legislative Assembly passed the AP Disha Bill on **13 December 2019**.
- **Name:** the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act 2023 is also called the **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam**.
- **Original limit:** Art. 334 first fixed SC/ST seat reservation for **10 years** (till 1960); later amendments extended it.
- **Part XVI (Arts. 330-342):** special provisions relating to certain classes (SCs, STs, Anglo-Indians, backward classes). Part XV = Elections; Part XVII = Official Language.
- **Why the PoA Act:** the PCR Act proved inadequate to check atrocities against SCs/STs, so Parliament enacted the PoA Act in 1989.
- **In force:** the PoA Amendment Act 2015 came into force in **2016** (26 January 2016).
- **INSTC route:** the main route goes by sea from Mumbai to **Bandar Abbas** port (Iran), then by road and rail through Iran and the Caspian region to Russia; Chabahar is being linked to it.
- **Navaratnalu period:** Navaratnalu was the YSRCP government's welfare package for **2019-24**.
- **Notification date:** the six Industries & Commerce 4.0 policies for 2024-29 were notified on **26 October 2024** and are valid for five years.
- **Birsa's Ulgulan – target:** it was directed against British land-grabbing, forced labour (beth begari) and the **dikus** (outside moneylenders, traders and landlords).

- **Critical Wildlife Habitat (FRA Sec. 2(b)):** areas of national parks and sanctuaries that must be **kept inviolate** for wildlife conservation, notified after an **open process of consultation** with the affected communities.
- **FRA implementation gaps:** focus on individual titles over **CFR** rights, **Gram Sabhas bypassed**, restrictive **MFP transit permits**, and **weak MoTA capacity** to push implementation.
- **MoEF circular (3 August 2009):** no forest diversion under the Forest Conservation Act until FRA rights are settled and **Gram Sabha consent** is obtained; it had no public-importance exception.
- **Dharti Aaba (DAJGUA) nodal ministry:** led by the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs**, which brings together the 17 line ministries.
- **PM-JANMAN full name:** Pradhan Mantri **Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan**; gives PVTGs housing, roads, water and electricity.
- **SHRESHTA portal:** seats for meritorious **SC students** in top **private residential schools**; online CBT registration (NETS by NTA), merit list and seat allotment.
- **PM Janjatiya Vikas Mission (TRIFED):** buys **MFP at MSP**, adds value (Van Dhan) and promotes **GI tags** for tribal products.
- **DACE beneficiaries:** the Dr Ambedkar Centres of Excellence give **free** Civil Services coaching to **SC students** in Central Universities.
- **UAPA, 1967:** India's main national-security law against **unlawful (disruptive) activities**, **unlawful associations** and **terror funding**.
- **Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada** are run under POSHAN Abhiyaan by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**.
- **Launch years:** **PMAY-Gramin – 2016** (from 1 April 2016, restructured from IAY); **PMAY-Urban – 2015**.
- **TRYSEM** (Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment) began on **15 August 1979**; later merged into SGSY (1999).
- **DAY-NULM** (2013) is run by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs** (earlier Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation).
- **Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi (AP):** financial help to SC students for higher studies abroad (overseas education).
- **Home Guards – purpose:** first raised in December 1946 to help the police control civil disturbance and communal riots.
- **Durkheim's *Le Suicide*:** published in **1897**; it gave the four types of suicide (egoistic, altruistic, anomic, fatalistic).
- **Chittoor Police:** ran **"Dharya Sparsa – Operation Flush-Out"** against drugs and illegal liquor (Jul 2026).
- **AP Economic Development Board (APEDB):** set up to speed up inclusive economic growth and bring investment into Andhra Pradesh.
- **Year:** The National Environment Policy was adopted in **2006**.
- **NAPCC:** The National Action Plan on Climate Change was released on **30 June 2008** with **eight** national missions.
- **National Food for Work Programme** – launched **14 November 2004** in the **150 most backward districts**; later merged into **NREGA** (2006).
- **Nigama Sabha (Satavahana period):** the body that ran city (town) administration in Satavahana times.
- **RRB share capital:** Centre 50%, sponsor bank 35%, State Government 15% (50:35:15).
- **NCDC and FPOs:** NCDC, an implementing agency of the 10,000 FPO scheme, promotes cooperative-sector FPOs through the PACS route.
- **e-Kisan Upaj Nidhi (4 March 2024):** a WDRA digital gateway that lets farmers get loans against e-NWRs of produce stored in WDRA-registered warehouses.

- **Commercialisation of agriculture:** when the area under non-food (cash) crops grows faster than the area under food crops, farming is becoming market-oriented – this is commercialisation of agriculture.
- **Real income from a price index:** Real national income = national income at current prices x 100 / price index (base year = 100). Example: Rs 30,000 crore x 100 / 150 = Rs 20,000 crore.
- **Rate of natural increase:** CBR minus CDR (per 1,000 population). Example: CBR 30 - CDR 10 = 20 per 1,000 = 2.0% a year.

- **Canals in the north:** Canal irrigation is strongest in the northern plains because the Himalayan rivers are perennial (snow-fed) and can feed canals all year; peninsular areas rely more on tanks.
- **Drip irrigation:** sends water straight to the root zone of plants; soluble fertiliser can be given through the same lines (fertigation).
- **Chemical pesticides:** act quickly with high efficacy; drawbacks are residues in food, harm to friendly insects and pest resistance, so IPM uses them only when needed.
- **Meghdoot app (2019):** mobile app that gives farmers weather-based agro-meteorological advisories in local languages.
- **PMKSY type:** an umbrella Centrally Sponsored Scheme launched in 2015-16 (1 July 2015), with AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Per Drop More Crop and Watershed components.
- **Tenant farmers' position (AP):** tenants pay rent and bear the production risk, but often have no land passbook, Kisan Credit Card (KCC) or crop insurance, so they miss formal credit and relief.
- **AP crop insurance from Rabi 2024-25:** enrolment under PMFBY/RWBCIS became voluntary; the farmer pays a small fixed share of the premium and the State and the Centre share the rest equally.

- **e-crop data gap:** insurance and relief in AP are given on the basis of e-crop booking, so actual cultivators (mostly tenants) missing from e-crop data can be left out of insurance and relief in a rainfall-deficit season.
- **Mundell-Fleming trilemma:** another name for the impossible trinity - a fixed exchange rate, free capital flows and an independent monetary policy cannot all be had together.
- **Other uses of AP e-PDS:** rice is also supplied through it to **Mid-Day Meal** schools and **Anganwadi centres**.
- **Ownership:** early **cotton mills** were mostly **Indian-owned** (Bombay, Ahmedabad); **jute mills** in Bengal were mostly **foreign (British)-owned**.
- **State PSUs:** AP has many State-level public enterprises, e.g. **APIIC** (industrial parks), **APSRTC** and **APGENCO**.
- **Why DFIs are needed:** banks take mostly short-term deposits, so lending long-term causes an asset-liability mismatch; DFIs fill this long-term finance gap.
- **Gold purity (carat):** pure gold is 24 carat, so 18 carat gold is 18/24 = 75% gold (22 carat = 91.6%).
- **Colonial deindustrialisation (Paul Bairoch):** India's share of world manufacturing output fell from about 24.5% (1750) to about 1.7% (1900).
- **Paradox of thrift (J.M. Keynes):** if everyone tries to save more at the same time, spending, income and output fall, so total saving may not rise.
- **Villament:** a new urban housing type in AP cities that combines a villa and an apartment – villa-like space inside an apartment building with shared apartment amenities.
- **M1–M4 framework (1977):** RBI introduced the money supply measures M1, M2, M3 and M4 on the recommendation of the **Second Working Group on Money Supply** (1977).
- **Calibrated tightening:** a stance in which rate cuts are off the table; rate hikes are measured and need not come at every meeting.
- **MUDRA full form:** Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency.
- **"Selling the family silver":** critics say disinvestment proceeds are used to bridge the fiscal deficit (meet current spending) instead of building new assets.
- **NIF management:** the NIF corpus is professionally managed (by selected public sector mutual funds) to give sustainable returns without reducing the corpus.

- **SARFAESI 2016 amendment and Sec 13(4):** the creditor threshold for the Sec 13(2) notice was **75%** of dues before the **2016** amendment cut it to **60%**; under **Sec 13(4)** lenders may take **possession** of the secured asset, **take over management** or **sell** it.

- **IBC concerns:** **deep haircuts** for lenders, **protracted litigation** that stretches timelines, and **NCLT capacity constraints** (too few benches and members); the Code has not removed guarantor liability.
- **BRIC origin:** the term **BRIC** was coined by **Jim O'Neill** (Goldman Sachs) in **2001**; the **first BRIC Summit** was held at **Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009**.
- **Greenshoe option:** an over-allotment option that lets the issuer sell **extra shares** (usually up to 15% of the issue) when demand is high.
- **Whole-time members:** of the **five other members** of the SEBI Board, **at least three are whole-time** members (SEBI Act, Section 4).
- **Credit-deposit ratio:** bank credit as a share of bank deposits; AP's **157.40%** means banks in the State **lent far more than the deposits** they raised there.
- **Incidence and elasticity:** if demand is **perfectly inelastic**, buyers do not cut purchases, so the price rises by the full tax and the **consumer bears the whole** indirect tax.
- **External strength:** ES 2025-26 saw the external sector as a strength - a low CAD (0.8% of GDP in H1 FY26) and forex reserves covering over 11 months of imports.
- **40% demerit slab (GST 2.0):** pan masala, tobacco products, aerated sugary drinks, large luxury cars, yachts and private aircraft for personal use, and online money gaming.
- **Largest share (15th FC, 2021-26):** **Uttar Pradesh** (about 17.9%), followed by Bihar (about 10.1%).
- **Grant dependence:** panchayats have limited powers to tax, so they depend substantially on **grants** (FC, SFC and CSS funds).
- Non-plan expenditure also included **subsidies** (food, fertiliser) and pensions.

- **Internal vs external debt:** classified by the **source** of borrowing. Internal debt is borrowed within the country (domestic economy); external debt comes from foreign sources, and foreign-currency obligations belong to it.
- **Progressive taxation:** the tax rate rises as income rises, so the rich pay more; this reduces inequality (distribution function).
- **Headline marker:** the **fiscal deficit** is the headline marker of fiscal health; revenue deficit and effective revenue deficit show what the borrowing is used for.
- **FRBM amendment 2018:** made **debt** the anchor with the **fiscal deficit** as the operational target, and **dropped the revenue deficit targets**.
- **Frontal inversion:** forms along a front, where warm air rides over a wedge of cold air, so temperature rises with height across the frontal boundary.
- **FDI push (2026):** AP is directing FDI to strategic sectors – **AI infrastructure, critical minerals, semiconductors, energy transition** and advanced technologies.
- **Rayalaseema hub:** Rayalaseema is being developed as an **automobile, steel, defence and space** hub (Kia, Royal Enfield, JSW Steel Kadapa, AMCA centre, Space City).
- **Other clearance portals:** **PARIVESH 3.0** (Union Environment Ministry) = environmental clearances; **E-Samudra** (DG Shipping, full launch Aug 2026) = digital maritime administration.
- **BRAP reform areas** (DPIIT) include the **single window system**, along with areas such as construction permits, labour and land.
- **VMRDA full form:** Visakhapatnam Metropolitan Region Development Authority (earlier VUDA, Visakhapatnam Urban Development Authority).
- **TUDA full form:** Tirupati Urban Development Authority, the urban development authority for Tirupati.
- **APIIC cluster types:** **Machilipatnam** = imitation jewellery cluster (Imitation Jewellery Park); **Makavarapalem** (Visakhapatnam) = alumina and aluminium industrial park.
- **CBIC node in AP:** **Krishnapatnam** (SPS Nellore) is the Andhra Pradesh node of the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor; NICDIT funds its trunk infrastructure.
- **Earth's twin:** Venus is called Earth's twin because it is close to the Earth in size, mass and density.
- **Meridians:** lines of longitude run north–south, from the North Pole to the South Pole.
- **Cities near the Tropic and their States:** Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar (Gujarat), Ujjain, Bhopal and Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh), Ranchi (Jharkhand), Agartala (Tripura), Aizawl (Mizoram).
- **Surface waves:** also called **L-waves** (long waves); they move along the surface, are the slowest and cause the most damage.
- **Asthenosphere:** lies in the **upper mantle**, about 100–200 km deep, just below the lithosphere.
- **Eduard Suess:** gave the terms SIAL, SIMA and NIFE, naming the Earth's layers after their main elements.
- **Markapur slate:** Markapur in Prakasam district is famous for its slate quarries and slate industry.
- **Krishna-Godavari (KG) basin:** the marine sediments of the Krishna and Godavari delta districts (Krishna, Eluru, Kakinada, Konaseema) hold AP's oil and natural gas.
- **Regur in Maharashtra:** Deccan Trap basalt covers most of the Maharashtra plateau, so Maharashtra has the largest area of black cotton (regur) soil.
- **Kamchatka earthquake (Aug 2025):** the M 8.8 megathrust quake struck off the Kamchatka Peninsula of **Russia**.
- **AP parent materials:** river silt of the **Godavari, Krishna and Pennar** is among the parent materials of Andhra Pradesh soils, along with the bedrock.
- **Muchchatla Chintamanu Gavi:** cave near Banaganapalle (Kurnool/Nandyal) known for **Upper Palaeolithic bone tools**.
- **Heatwaves and ozone:** heatwaves raise **ground-level ozone**; north-west India and the Indo-Gangetic Plain are badly affected.

- **Indian Cyclone Intensity Scale:** the IMD classifies North Indian Ocean systems on this scale, from Low Pressure Area and Depression up to Super Cyclonic Storm (Saffir-Simpson is used for hurricanes).
- **Geo-informatics in cyclones:** satellite data and GIS help predict a cyclone's track and intensity and plan evacuations.
- **Services GVA, 2014-15 (current prices):** about **₹2.15 lakh crore**, about 44% of AP's GVA.
- **India (ISFR 2023):** forest cover **21.76%** of geographical area; forest + tree cover **25.17%**.
- **Formation (1 November 1956):** undivided Andhra Pradesh was formed with **20 districts**.
- **Dharali-Harsil (5 Aug 2025):** a **flash flood** hit Dharali-Harsil in Uttarkashi after an ice patch collapsed on the Srikanta glacier.
- **NDMA avalanche guidelines:** cover both **structural** measures (snow nets, snow bridges, galleries) and **non-structural** measures (hazard zonation, early warning, training).
- **Types of mitigation:** **avoidance**, **minimization** and **compensatory** mitigation.
- **Hazard-specific control activity:** a measure aimed at one particular hazard, e.g. building **flood levees** against floods.
- **Findlater Current:** flows in the **western Arabian Sea**, along the Somali coast (Horn of Africa); it reverses with the monsoon.

- **Deep Ocean Mission components:** one of the nine PM-STIAC missions; covers deep-sea mining and a manned submersible, ocean climate advisory services, deep-sea biodiversity, deep ocean survey and exploration, energy and freshwater from the ocean, and a marine station for ocean biology.
- **Ruwenzori:** a major range of Africa on the Uganda–DR Congo border ("Mountains of the Moon"); the Atlas and Drakensberg are the other major African ranges.
- **Lake Malawi** is also called **Lake Nyasa**; Lake Victoria (Victoria Nyanza) is a different lake.
- **Black Sea:** an inland sea between **south-eastern Europe, the Caucasus and Anatolia**; it reaches the Mediterranean through the Turkish Straits (Bosphorus, Sea of Marmara, Dardanelles).
- **Adriatic Sea:** an arm of the **Mediterranean** between Italy and the Balkans.
- **Red sanders belt:** the Seshachalam, Palakonda and Veligonda ranges form part of the **southern Eastern Ghats**; red sanders is endemic to this belt.
- **Extent of the Eastern Ghats:** they are also described as running about 1,750 km between the **Mahanadi** and the **Vaigai** rivers (Odisha to Tamil Nadu).
- **Dandakaranya:** a highland of the **central-eastern** part of the Peninsula (Chhattisgarh–Odisha–Andhra Pradesh region).
- **Order of the Punjab rivers (north to south / west to east):** Jhelum → Chenab → Ravi → Beas → Sutlej.
- **Ken-Betwa and Panna:** the link's Daudhan dam on the Ken lies inside the **Panna Tiger Reserve** (MP), so the project passes through Panna.
- **Arthashastra:** Kautilya's Arthashastra has a section on measures against famine, such as storing grain and relief works.
- **LEADS full form:** Logistics Ease Across Different States; it ranks Indian States and UTs on logistics, while the World Bank LPI ranks countries.
- **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR):** deaths of infants before their first birthday per 1,000 live births; deaths before the fifth birthday give the under-5 mortality rate.
- **NHDR 2001 – lowest State:** **Bihar** was at the bottom of the first NHDR of India (2001), while **Kerala** was at the top.
- **India (PLFS 2023-24):** about **46.1%** of India's workers were in agriculture; AP's 45.6% is slightly below it.
- **Kondapalli chromite:** The chromite of the **Kondapalli Hills** in AP lies in the old **Krishna district** (now NTR district).
- **Critical Mineral Recycling Incentive Scheme:** a **Central Sector scheme** under NCMM (Cabinet, Sep 2025; Rs 1,500 crore); covers e-waste, lithium-ion battery scrap and other scrap.
- **NCMM tools:** it encourages **PSUs and private firms to acquire critical mineral assets abroad** and plans a **National Critical Mineral Stockpile**.
- **Nickname:** AP is called **'Ratna Garbha'** (womb of gems) for its rich and varied mineral deposits.
- **ANI and ASI:** the 2009 genetic study named the two ancestral groups of Indians **Ancestral North Indians (ANI)** and **Ancestral South Indians (ASI)**.
- **Criticism of old schemes:** older racial schemes (Risley, Guha) relied on visible physical traits and colonial ethnography; modern genetics shows such rigid racial categories are not scientific.
- **Western Brachycephals - regions:** Alpinoid and Dinaric types are found in Gujarat, Bengal, Odisha and Coorg; the Armenoid type in the Parsis.
- **SEZ examples by State:** Vallarpadam (Kochi) SEZ is in **Kerala**; Nanguneri SEZ (Tirunelveli district) is in **Tamil Nadu**.
- **NH-44 route:** passes through Delhi, Agra, Jhansi, Nagpur, Hyderabad and Bengaluru; Pune is on NH-48 and NH-65, not NH-44.
- **Modified UDAN (Budget 2025-26):** to connect **120 new destinations** and carry **4 crore passengers** in the next 10 years.
- **LEADS** = **Logistics Ease Across Different States**; ranks States on logistics performance; released since **2018**.
